why: The Checkpoint an actor carries in its Temporal activity heartbeat, and the resume it implies.
note: THE COMMIT MAP USED TO LIVE IN REDIS, under a 24h TTL, in a hash that `volatile-lru` evicted
first (ADR 0059). A checkpoint in the heartbeat lives in the activity's own history instead, so
it survives anything the cache does — but only if both SDKs encode it identically, because the
writer of a checkpoint and its reader are often different processes and sometimes different
`done` IS A RANGE SET BECAUSE A HEARTBEAT IS SMALL. A batch of 10,000 units with every unit
committed is one range, not ten thousand integers. Temporal's payload limit applies to heartbeat
details, so a per-unit list is a batch size ceiling in disguise.
CANONICAL FORM IS PART OF THE CONTRACT, not an optimisation: inclusive [lo,hi] pairs, sorted
ascending, merged so no two ranges touch or overlap (hi + 1 < next.lo). Two implementations that
agree on membership and disagree on encoding produce different bytes for the same facts, and the
comparison that would have caught it is the one nobody runs.

canonical.why: empty is empty — not [[0,0]], which would claim unit 0 committed
one index is a one-wide inclusive range
a contiguous run collapses to one range
insertion order must not change the encoding — this is the drift that matters
ADJACENT RANGES MERGE. [0,2] and [3,5] touch, so they are one range, not two
a single index bridging two ranges merges all three
re-adding a committed index is a no-op, because a retry re-commits what it re-ran
re-adding inside an existing range changes nothing
one gap of exactly one index does NOT merge — off by one here loses a unit
a large sparse set stays compact where it can

members.why: membership inside, at both edges, and outside
an empty set contains nothing, including 0
a one-wide range contains exactly its index

wire.why: THE BYTES, not just the values. A writer that renders done as [{"lo":0,"hi":1}] agrees on every membership question and is unreadable to its peers. Compact JSON, keys in this order.
an empty set is [] and not null — different bytes, and a strict decoder tells them apart
failed is SORTED, because a Go map iterates randomly and an unsorted list makes two encodings of one checkpoint differ

resume.why: nothing committed: every unit is still to do
a prefix committed: resume after it
a hole in the middle is re-run, because a gap means it never committed
an ISOLATED unit is not re-run — it is a decided failure, and re-running it re-poisons the scope
everything accounted for: nothing to do, and the batch is finished

A CHECKPOINT FROM A DIFFERENT BATCH IS DISCARDED ENTIRELY. Unit indices are positions within one batch, so honouring a stale checkpoint would skip units by index in a batch that never ran them — silent data loss, and the exact failure a plain index list invites
an empty batch_id matches nothing, including another empty one — an unidentified checkpoint is not evidence
A FUTURE VERSION IS REFUSED, NOT PARTIALLY UNDERSTOOD. A v2 that added a field a v1 reader ignores would have the v1 reader resume from a checkpoint it only half read
version 0 or absent is not v1 either — it is an encoder that did not say, which is the same risk
done beyond the batch is ignored rather than refused: a shorter re-dispatch of the same batch id is a bug upstream, and dropping the run over it would turn a recoverable confusion into an outage
a zero-unit batch has nothing to do and is not an error
